key_insight: A fully discrete finite element scheme for Kirchhoff-type equations achieves optimal spatial accuracy and second-order time accuracy while exactly preserving discrete energy for homogeneous, constant-coefficient problems.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of nonlinear, nonlocal dynamics relevant to structural mechanics, with energy conservation in a restricted setting.
method: Conforming finite elements of arbitrary polynomial degree p in two spatial dimensions.
Picard iteration for the nonlinearity, supported by convergence and error analysis.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution experiments reproduce second-order temporal convergence and the predicted h^(p+1) spatial convergence in L².
watch_item: Exact discrete-energy preservation is established only for the homogeneous, constant-coefficient case; convergence and error guarantees depend on the analysis hypotheses.
paper_title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
